key_insight: Decision2Care performed diagnostic work-ups without generating text, recording candidate actions, probabilities, and execution rules for audit.
clinical_relevance: Auditable action records could help clinicians examine how an AI assessment changed, but clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Assign probabilities to permitted electronic health record actions.
Execute the highest-probability action using fixed rules.
Track diagnostic options and probability changes throughout each work-up.
evidence_signal: Across records from 546 emergency admissions covering 12 diseases, Decision2Care achieved 86.5% diagnostic accuracy versus MIRA-v2’s 86.1%, with a median work-up time of 2.2 seconds versus 92–100 seconds.
watch_item: Evaluation used existing patient records; prospective safety and workflow impact remain uncertain, and four high-confidence errors were traced to individual imaging reports.
paper_title: Auditable Clinical Support with Decision Agents
